manual_deterministic_project_gate.reason: These are deliberate task-level orchestration entrypoints, not lightweight unit tests; the script-test aggregate must validate their ownership without silently running long nested suites.
conditions: an operator or task-specific gate explicitly selects the driver
the driver's own fail-closed preflight succeeds
resources: the existing locked repository source tree
the already-provisioned project runtimes selected by the driver

manual_specialized_contract_environment.reason: These drivers intentionally run inside the separately locked Browser Use contract environment, which the backend script-test interpreter cannot impersonate.
conditions: the specialized contract environment already exists at its repository-owned path
an operator explicitly selects the driver
resources: tools/browser-use-contract/.venv
the locked Browser Use contract source and fixtures

manual_real_cloud_or_account.reason: These paths can consume paid model or cloud APIs, signed cloud storage, or an authorized platform account; a default aggregate must never spend money or act under credentials.
conditions: the driver-specific real-cloud opt-in is explicit
the authorized operator supplies only the credentials and account named by the driver
the operator accepts the driver's bounded cost and cleanup plan
resources: authorized short-lived model or cloud credentials
the driver-specific bucket, account, or private browser Profile
the existing desktop, browser, and project build runtimes

manual_embedded_browser_native.reason: These drivers stage the real digest-locked embedded Chromium for the current supported macOS or Windows target; they require an explicit native artifact run instead of an automatic source-shape test.
conditions: the host matches one of the driver-supported native macOS or Windows target IDs
the locked archive is already present at the repository archive_path() location
the operator explicitly selects the driver and its cleanup scope
resources: the existing digest-locked Chrome for Testing archive
the matching native Node, Rust, and application build toolchains
isolated temporary browser Profiles and package roots

manual_embedded_browser_macos.reason: These drivers explicitly limit their real staging, concurrency, or release-package evidence to macOS; running their source readers on another platform cannot satisfy that evidence.
conditions: the host matches the macOS architecture accepted by the selected driver
the locked archive is already present at the repository archive_path() location
the operator explicitly selects the driver and its cleanup scope
resources: the existing digest-locked macOS Chrome for Testing archive
macOS Node, Rust, application, and package build toolchains
isolated temporary browser Profiles and package roots

manual_embedded_browser_windows.reason: These drivers need a native Windows browser or NSIS packaging boundary and cannot be made truthful by reading their source on macOS.
conditions: the host is native non-elevated Windows with the required architecture
the locked browser archive is already present
the operator explicitly selects the driver and its cleanup scope
resources: the existing Windows Chrome for Testing archive
Windows Node, Rust, NSIS, and PowerShell build tools
isolated LOCALAPPDATA, Profile, and package directories

manual_hidden_desktop_app.reason: These drivers build and launch dedicated hidden Tauri Apps and WebDriver sessions; they are safe only as explicit desktop acceptances, not as surprise script-test work.
conditions: a supported desktop session is available
the driver-specific ports and private AppData roots are free
an operator explicitly accepts the build duration
resources: the existing frontend Node modules and Rust target cache
a native Tauri/WebDriver desktop session
isolated AppData and browser Profile directories

manual_media_evidence.reason: The acceptance result depends on a real media artifact supplied outside the source tree; a missing artifact is a blocked run, not a passing structural test.
conditions: the operator supplies the exact driver-owned evidence environment variable
the media was produced by the required real path and is safe to inspect
resources: a real acceptance video or readiness evidence artifact
the existing media inspection and desktop runtimes

manual_packaged_executor.reason: These drivers freeze, sign, supervise, or audit native Executor/App artifacts; source readers cannot prove the packaged process boundary.
conditions: the host is one of the native platforms accepted by the selected driver
the existing build caches and platform signing test material are available
an operator explicitly selects the artifact build and cleanup
resources: the existing backend virtual environment and PyInstaller inputs
native Rust and platform packaging tools
isolated package, AppData, and process roots

manual_postgresql_network.reason: These drivers own isolated PostgreSQL/Uvicorn/WebSocket lifecycle and therefore require deliberate container and port allocation.
conditions: the repository Compose runtime is available
the driver can reserve its isolated ports, network, and volumes
an operator explicitly selects the integration run
resources: Docker Compose and the existing postgres-test image
the existing backend virtual environment
isolated loopback ports, networks, and volumes

manual_full_desktop_stack.reason: These paths combine isolated PostgreSQL and Control Plane state with a hidden Tauri App or packaged Executor; they are full-stack acceptances with bounded but material runtime cost.
conditions: Docker, native desktop, and loopback prerequisites all pass
the driver-specific App identity and AppData roots are unused
an operator explicitly selects the full-stack run and cleanup
resources: Docker Compose and isolated PostgreSQL
the existing backend, Node, Rust, and Tauri environments
isolated ports, AppData, Executor state, and browser Profiles

manual_authorized_private_profile.reason: This real read-only platform probe needs an explicitly authorized App-private login Profile; an aggregate must never discover or reuse a user's default Profile.
conditions: the operator supplies AUTOMATION_TOOL_D616_PROFILE_DIRECTORY explicitly
the Profile is App-private, authorized, and not concurrently open
the operator accepts the platform's read-only risk controls
resources: one authorized App-private Douyin browser Profile
the installed system browser and existing backend environment

manual_material_video_candidate.reason: These drivers build or launch a real frozen material-video Worker and, for App paths, a native hidden desktop build; the candidate must be staged explicitly.
conditions: the locked material-video source and existing build environment are present
the host supports the selected frozen Worker and App path
an operator explicitly selects the candidate build and cleanup
resources: the existing material-video source, Python environment, and freezer inputs
native Node, Rust, and Tauri tools where required
isolated Worker, WebUI, workspace, and AppData roots
